clue.text: Sound of bee, insect seen as sweet

parts.note: a bee hums as it flies
a bug is a small insect

explanation.surface: A buzzing bee and another creature are regarded as something sweet.
explanation.walkthrough: A humbug is a British boiled mint sweet, usually striped.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a humbug is a hard striped peppermint confection sold in British sweet shops.

clue.text: Habitual practice of superior person adjudged wise

parts.note: U means upper-class or superior, as in U and non-U
a sage is a person thought wise

explanation.surface: The custom of a top person reckoned wise.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: established custom or habitual way of doing things.

clue.text: One smashing glass — first of robbers to enter

indicators.note: the robbers' letter goes into the glass

parts.note: a beaker is a drinking glass

indicators.note: takes only the opening letter of the word robbers

explanation.surface: Someone smashes a window, the first of the robbers to get in.
explanation.definitionFit: Literal: something that breaks or smashes, as a wave or a vandal.

clue.text: Georgia's idle talk

parts.note: GA is the US postal abbreviation for the state of Georgia; the possessive ending supplies the S
the apostrophe-s ending of the word Georgia's gives this letter

explanation.surface: Gossip from the state of Georgia.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang: gas is chatter or empty talk.

clue.text: Most vile street east of HQ

indicators.note: in an across entry, east is to the right, so the street piece follows the headquarters piece

parts.note: headquarters is a base of operations

explanation.surface: A grim street lies just east of some headquarters.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: base means low and contemptible, and the superlative means the most despicable.

clue.text: Expert on plants and animals

parts.note: a buff is an enthusiast or expert
aloes are succulent plants

explanation.surface: A naturalist who knows about flora and fauna.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: buffalo are large wild oxen, a kind of animal.

clue.text: Man getting covered in black makes son cry

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for son in genealogies
to weep is to cry

explanation.surface: A sooty man reduces a boy to tears.
explanation.walkthrough: A chimney sweep gets black with soot.
explanation.definitionFit: Cryptic description: a chimney cleaner gets covered in soot.

clue.text: Worker dealing with sheep — hers are awkward

indicators.note: something awkward is out of shape, so these letters are put in a different order

explanation.surface: A farmhand handles sheep, and her ones are difficult.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: someone who clips the fleece off sheep.

clue.text: A device to stop someone having hard drink?

definitions.text: A device to stop someone having hard drink?

parts.words: A device to stop someone having hard drink?
parts.note: hard drink suggests spirits, but here it is hard water, which a household appliance treats by removing calcium

explanation.surface: Something that keeps a person off the strong liquor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hard drink' looks like alcohol; read literally it is drinking water full of minerals.
explanation.definitionFit: A cryptic description of an appliance that removes limescale-forming minerals from mains supply.

clue.text: Feeble few days by the sound of it

indicators.note: says the word for the days is to be heard rather than spelt, giving its same-sounding twin

parts.note: seven days make a week

explanation.surface: Someone sounds feeble after a few days.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: feeble and lacking strength mean the same.

clue.text: People in tents imbibing hot alcoholic drink

indicators.note: drinking in, so the tent-dwellers take the hot letter inside them

parts.note: campers sleep in tents
H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps

explanation.surface: Holidaymakers under canvas drink something hot and boozy.
explanation.walkthrough: Champers is British slang for champagne.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang: champers is the jokey British word for champagne, a sparkling wine.

clue.text: Amenable, making calm point after negotiation

indicators.note: negotiation reshapes positions, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone is agreeable after talks make a calm point.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: willing to go along with requests, obedient.

clue.text: A quiet animal in retreat

parts.note: sh is the call for quiet
a ram is a male sheep, an animal

explanation.surface: A silent creature hides away in a retreat.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: an ashram is a Hindu religious retreat or hermitage.

clue.text: Home Counties prize coming to coastal area?

parts.note: the Home Counties around London lie in the South East, SE
an award is a prize

explanation.surface: A prize from the counties near London heads to the seaside.
explanation.walkthrough: The Home Counties are the English counties surrounding London.
explanation.definitionFit: Direction: heading towards the sea, hence towards the shore.

clue.text: Happens to be officer commanding despicable people

parts.note: OC is the military abbreviation for officer commanding
curs are contemptible people, from the word for mongrel dogs

explanation.surface: A commanding officer turns out to be in charge of rotters.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: something that takes place or comes about.

clue.text: Wanted mixed school to have internal check

indicators.note: the school holds the check piece within it

parts.note: a coed school takes boys and girls
to vet is to check

explanation.surface: A desired co-educational school with an inspection on site.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: craved or desired, as a prize others want.

clue.text: Labyrinth constructor lauded as innovatory

indicators.note: something innovatory makes things new, so these letters are rearranged into a fresh order

explanation.surface: The maze-builder is praised as a pioneer.
explanation.walkthrough: In Greek myth Daedalus built the Labyrinth for King Minos of Crete.
explanation.definitionFit: Mythology: the Athenian craftsman who designed the Cretan maze housing the Minotaur.

clue.text: Doctor, I have a road up to the house

definitions.text: a road up to the house

parts.note: 've is the contracted form of have

explanation.surface: A doctor says he has a road to his house.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a private road or driveway leading to a house.

clue.text: Blade — one associated with blood, we hear

indicators.note: says the blood vessel is heard, not spelt, giving its same-sounding twin

parts.note: a vein carries blood back to the heart

explanation.surface: A knife blade apparently connected with bloodshed.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a vane is a flat blade of a windmill, propeller or turbine.

clue.text: Relation of a German set up English church

indicators.note: in a down entry, set up means written upwards, so the German word is read backwards

parts.note: ein is German for a
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A German relative establishes an English church.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a niece is a family member, a sibling's daughter.

clue.text: London landlord? One may be starting a sentence

definitions.meaning: playfully, someone who lets property in the capital city

definitions.text: One may be starting a sentence
definitions.meaning: the first letter of a sentence is upper case

explanation.surface: A city landlord who might be starting a prison term.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sentence' hints at prison; it is a written sentence.
explanation.definitionFit: Pun and plain sense: an upper-case letter begins a sentence, and a capital-city letter of rooms.

clue.text: Past fifty, old boy to send up

indicators.note: the old boy comes past, after, the fifty

parts.note: L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: An old boy over fifty sends something skyward.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: to lob is to throw or hit a ball high in the air.

clue.text: Notice opening period leading up to Christmas

parts.note: an ad is a notice or advertisement
a vent is an opening for air

explanation.surface: An advertisement launches the pre-Christmas season.
explanation.definitionFit: Church calendar: the season of the four Sundays before Christmas Day.

clue.text: Does it spread bovine TB? Bother!

definitions.meaning: the wild animal blamed in Britain for passing tuberculosis to cattle

explanation.surface: An exasperated question about whether something spreads cattle disease.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain the badger is controversially culled as a carrier of bovine TB.
explanation.definitionFit: Verb sense: to pester someone persistently; the animal sense refers to a black-and-white burrowing mammal.
